officialTitle: Phase II study of carboplatin and paclitaxel in advanced thymoma and thymic carcinoma
setting: Advanced previously untreated thymoma and thymic carcinoma

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: From February 2001 through January 2008, 46 patients were enrolled.
design.notes: Single-arm prospective multicentre phase II trial with separate thymoma (n = 21) and thymic carcinoma (n = 23) cohorts. Non-comparative evidence.

clinicalQuestion: What is the activity of carboplatin plus paclitaxel in advanced, previously untreated thymoma and thymic carcinoma?

pico.population: Unresectable, previously untreated thymoma or thymic carcinoma
pico.intervention: Carboplatin AUC 6 plus paclitaxel 225 mg/m2 every 3 weeks, up to six cycles
pico.outcomes: Primary: objective response rate. PFS, OS, toxicity

arms.label: Thymoma cohort
arms.dosing: Carboplatin AUC 6 plus paclitaxel 225 mg/m2 every 3 weeks, maximum six cycles
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were treated with carboplatin (area under the curve, 6) plus paclitaxel (225 mg/m(2)) every 3 weeks for a maximum of six cycles.

arms.label: Thymic carcinoma cohort
arms.dosing: Carboplatin AUC 6 plus paclitaxel 225 mg/m2 every 3 weeks, maximum six cycles
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were treated with carboplatin (area under the curve, 6) plus paclitaxel (225 mg/m(2)) every 3 weeks for a maximum of six cycles.

publications.title: Phase II study of carboplatin and paclitaxel in advanced thymoma and thymic carcinoma.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Using RECIST (Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors) 1.0 criteria, three complete responses (CRs) and six partial responses (PRs; objective response rate [ORR], 42.9%; 90% CI, 24.5% to 62.8%) were observed in the thymoma cohort; 10 patients had stable disease.
For patients with thymic carcinoma, no CRs and five PRs (ORR, 21.7%; 90% CI, 9.0% to 40.4%) were observed; 12 patients had stable disease.
Progression-free survival (PFS) was 16.7 (95% CI, 7.2 to 19.8) and 5.0 (95% CI, 3.0 to 8.3) months for thymoma and thymic carcinoma cohorts, respectively.
Progression-free survival (PFS) was 16.7 (95% CI, 7.2 to 19.8) and 5.0 (95% CI, 3.0 to 8.3) months for thymoma and thymic carcinoma cohorts, respectively.
Median survival time was 20.0 months (95% CI, 5.0 to 43.6 months) for patients with thymic carcinoma, but it has not been reached for patients with thymoma.

safety.description: Grade 4 or greater toxicity, mostly neutropenia (number of patients)
safety.sourceQuote: Thirteen patients had grade 4 or greater toxicity, mostly neutropenia.

strengths: Prospective multicentre trial with separate histology cohorts
limitations: Single-arm phase II evidence with small cohorts; no comparator
Wide confidence intervals around response rates
Authors judged activity possibly lower than expected with anthracycline-based therapy, but without direct comparison

clinicalImplications.text: Single-arm phase II data showing moderate activity of carboplatin-paclitaxel in both thymoma and thymic carcinoma, with clearly poorer outcomes in thymic carcinoma; it is a commonly used anthracycline-free option, especially for thymic carcinoma.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Always separate thymoma from thymic carcinoma when quoting outcomes: in this trial PFS and survival were markedly worse for thymic carcinoma.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 21502559. Registry ID not printed in abstract. Cooperative group affiliation not stated in the abstract.
